turns.user: For a 3DCP mortar with w/b 0.35, s/b 1.5, 90 % OPC + 10 % silica fume and 0.6 % PCE, plot the Bingham flow curve up to 100 1/s and the structuration curve over 45 minutes of rest, and compare both with measured literature curves.
turns.text:
I’ll check the mix conventions, predict the flow and structuration curves, and retrieve measured literature curves for comparison.
Created both plots with literature overlays and q10–q90 uncertainty bands:

- **Bingham flow:** [Plot](<C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-165944-9997/flow_curve_OPC90_SF10_PCE06.png>) · [CSV](<C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-165944-9997/flow_curve_OPC90_SF10_PCE06.csv>)
- **Structuration:** [Plot](<C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-165944-9997/structuration_OPC90_SF10_PCE06.png>) · [CSV](<C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-165944-9997/structuration_OPC90_SF10_PCE06.csv>)

| Predicted quantity | q50 [q10, q90] |
|---|---:|
| Dynamic yield stress | 234 [16, 843] Pa |
| Plastic viscosity | 6.43 [0.84, 33.13] Pa·s |
| Shear stress at 100 s⁻¹ | 1,023 [250, 3,901] Pa |
| Initial static yield stress | 271 [22, 9,125] Pa |
| Structuration rate | 0.697 [0.023, 13.669] Pa/s |
| Static yield stress after 45 min | 4,003 [307, 61,123] Pa |

The curves use \(\tau=\tau_0+\mu\dot\gamma\) and \(\tau_s=\tau_{s0}+A_{\mathrm{thix}}t\). Pointwise quantiles come from sampled parameter distributions; they need not equal curves constructed from parameter medians.

**Literature comparison.** The flow overlays include [published silica-fume mortars](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2021.104158) at w/b 0.35 and s/b 1. Their stresses at 100 s⁻¹ are 202.2 Pa for 6% silica fume and 309.17 Pa for 10%—below the predicted median. These overlays reconstruct the authors’ fitted Bingham equations, rather than raw measured points. The [NZ-0 overlay](https://doi.org/10.3390/buildings16030490) uses digitized measured flow curves.

The structuration overlays are digitized measurements for [R20, R40 and R60](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2024.105509). Their recorded stress ranges are respectively 2,080–3,650, 970–2,130 and 170–1,080 Pa over 10–60 minutes. **Their clock starts at water addition, not at the start of rest**, so they provide qualitative context rather than a matched validation.

The structuration-rate model is weak: treat its curve as **order-of-magnitude guidance**, with the published measurements as primary evidence. Experimental verification is needed.

Defaults: natural sand; PCE interpreted as product mass relative to binder; initial rest time zero. The tool also populated age 28 d, `comp_cube50`, and moist curing at 20 °C/95% RH; these are metadata defaults, not a fresh-rheology test protocol.
